newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI Australia says targets niches in Asia.
newsitem.headline: ICI Australia says targets niches in Asia.

text.p: Chemicals group ICI Australia Ltd said on Monday growth earmarked for its Asian operations would be targeted at areas such as paints and explosives where the company believed it has advantages over its competition.

The company's managing director Philip Weickhardt told a media briefing ICI Australia believed it had significant opportunities to grow sales of explosives, water treatment chemicals and consumer items such as textured, protective and powdered coatings in Asia.
"We have unique strengths here where we will have opportunities," Weickhardt said.
Weickhardt said ICI Australia's expansion into Asia following the exit of its major shareholder, ICI Plc, would be "focused and targeted".
"In terms of our growth into Asia, we are mindful of generating generating profits and returns. We are going to focus on areas we genuinely think we can earn superior returns," he said.
Expansion into Asia was often a slow process, Weickhardt said. He said ICI Australia had been examining the possibility of building an ammonium nitrate plant in Indonesia for the past four years.
"We are still hopeful we will do that. These projects take time."
ICI Plc offloaded the bulk of its 62.4 percent stake through a public offer to institutions and retail investors. The offer closed oversubscribed last week.

ICI Australia has negotiated 31 agreements with its former parent which allow it to compete with ICI Plc in any market with the exception of the explosives, refinished paints and canned coating areas.
For its explosives division, ICI Australia negotiated a wider area for its operations that included all of the Asia/Pacific region east of India.
